title: Τεχνητή νοημοσύνη και πράσινο μάρκετινγκ: Μια συστηματική βιβλιογραφική ανασκόπηση
abstract: Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία διερευνά τον ρόλο της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης στο πεδίο του πράσινου μάρκετινγκ, μέσω της μεθοδολογίας της Συστηματικής Βιβλιογραφικής Ανασκόπησης. Στόχος της μελέτης είναι η συστηματική καταγραφή, αξιολόγηση και σύνθεση της διεθνούς επιστημονικής βιβλιογραφίας σχετικά με τις εφαρμογές της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης σε στρατηγικές βιώσιμου και πράσινου μάρκετινγκ, τις επιδράσεις τους στη βιώσιμη καταναλωτική συμπεριφορά και τη συμβολή τους στη λήψη επιχειρηματικών αποφάσεων. Για την επιλογή των μελετών εφαρμόστηκε το πρωτόκολλο PRISMA, αξιοποιώντας τις βάσεις δεδομένων Scopus και Web of Science, με στόχο τη διαμόρφωση ενός αξιόπιστου τελικού δείγματος δημοσιεύσεων. Το τελικό δείγμα περιλαμβάνει 45 επιστημονικές δημοσιεύσεις. Η ανάλυση των δεδομένων πραγματοποιήθηκε με βιβλιομετρική χαρτογράφηση στο λογισμικό VOSviewer, καθώς και με θεματική ανάλυση του περιεχομένου των επιλεγμένων μελετών. Τα αποτελέσματα αναδεικνύουν βασικές θεματικές κατευθύνσεις της βιβλιογραφίας, όπως η χρήση της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης σε στρατηγικές πράσινου μάρκετινγκ, η επίδρασή της στη βιώσιμη καταναλωτική συμπεριφορά και ο ρόλος του πράσινου μάρκετινγκ ως συνδετικού μηχανισμού μεταξύ βιωσιμότητας, τεχνολογίας και καταναλωτικών επιλογών. Από την ανάλυση προκύπτει ότι η επίδραση της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης και του πράσινου μάρκετινγκ στη βιώσιμη καταναλωτική συμπεριφορά δεν είναι ίδια σε όλες τις περιπτώσεις, καθώς εξαρτάται από παράγοντες όπως η εμπιστοσύνη, η αξιοπιστία των περιβαλλοντικών μηνυμάτων και οι αντιλήψεις των καταναλωτών. title: Multimodal Classification of Parotid Tumors – A Proof of Concept
abstract: Abstract Preoperative differentiation between benign and malignant parotid tumors is challenging but can influence treatment and outcome. In this proof-of-concept study, we investigated multimodal AI-based classification combining clinical tabular data and ultrasound images, comparing unimodal and multimodal approaches for binary benign-malignant classification. The study included 594 patients with parotid tumors (449 benign, 145 malignant) after preprocessing. The image-only classifier achieved 0.73 accuracy at image level and 0.75 after patient-level aggregation. The tabular model reached 0.88 accuracy, while the multimodal model maintained this accuracy with a slightly improved weighted F1- score (0.89) and malignant recall of 0.93. These results suggest that image-derived features provided complementary information, primarily improving sensitivity for malignant tumors.

title: Detection of causality in sentences: a comparative study of ensemble and non-ensemble approaches across embedding paradigms with explainable AI
abstract: Detection of causality in sentences aims to identify causal relationships expressed in natural language text. This task is critical for applications in finance, healthcare, safety, business risk management, scientific literature, and policy making. In this study, we present a comprehensive comparative analysis of causality detection using ensemble and non-ensemble approaches. The ensemble framework integrates Random Forest, Naive Bayes, XGBoost, and Linear Support Vector Machines with soft and weighted-soft voting. To evaluate effectiveness, experiments are grouped into three categories: (i) traditional embeddings (TF-IDF, Bag-of-Words, Word2Vec, FastText, GloVe), (ii) deep learning architectures (CNN, LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, CNN-GRU, CNN-LSTM), and (iii) transformer-based embeddings (BERT, RoBERTa, BART, MiniLM, DistilBERT, DeBERTa). For broader comparison, non-ensemble baselines include Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Neural Tangent Kernel for traditional embeddings, while SVM-RBF is used for deep learning and transformer embeddings. Evaluations are conducted on four publicly available datasets using F1-score, precision, accuracy, recall, and ROC-AUC with tuning hyperparameter (for non-ensemble approach) and 10-fold cross-validation. Results show that ensemble-based approaches consistently outperform non-ensemble methods, achieving F1-scores of 99.98%, 98.38%, 99.72%, and 99.99% on the four datasets. Finally, explainable AI techniques (LIME, Anchor, Counterfactuals) are employed to interpret model decisions, providing insights into causality detection mechanisms.

title: Compiling Quantum Regular Language States
abstract: State preparation compilers for quantum computers typically sit at two extremes: general-purpose routines that treat the target as an opaque amplitude vector, and bespoke constructions for a handful of well-known state families. We ask whether a compiler can instead accept simple, structure-aware specifications while providing predictable resource guarantees. We answer this by designing and implementing a quantum state-preparation compiler for regular language states (RLS): uniform superpositions over bitstrings accepted by a regular description, and their complements. Users describe the target state via (i) a finite set of bitstrings, (ii) a regular expression, or (iii) a deterministic finite automaton (DFA), optionally with a complement flag. By translating the input to a DFA, minimizing it, and mapping it to an optimal matrix product state (MPS), the compiler obtains an intermediate representation (IR) that exposes and compresses hidden structure. The efficient DFA representation and minimization offloads expensive linear algebra computation in exchange of simpler automata manipulations. The combination of the regular-language frontend and this IR gives concise specifications not only for RLS but also for their complements that might otherwise require exponentially large state descriptions. This enables state preparation of an RLS or its complement with the same asymptotic resources and compile time, which to our knowledge is not supported by existing compilers. We outline two hardware-aware backends: SeqRLSP, which yields linear-depth, ancilla-free circuits for linear nearest-neighbor architectures via sequential generation, and TreeRLSP, which achieves logarithmic depth on all-to-all connectivity via a tree tensor network. On the theory side, we prove circuit-depth and gate-count bounds that scale with the system size and the maximal Schmidt rank of the target state, and we give compile-time bounds that expose the benefit of the initial DFA representation. We implement the full pipeline and evaluate it on Dicke and W states, random uniform superpositions, and complement states, comparing against general-purpose, sparse-state, and specialized baselines.

title: Exposing the Cost of Deep Learning Audio Development
abstract: The environmental impact of deep learning has attracted increasing attention over the past decade. Existing studies mainly focus on the energy and carbon emissions of model training and inference, while the whole development phase is often overlooked. Yet, architecture prototyping and intensive experiments are conducted during this stage, which is highly energy-demanding. In this article, we propose a methodology to estimate these costs, based on activity logs from the Grid5000 shared computing platform used by the LORIA laboratory. As a case-study, we focus on audio projects developed in the Multispeech research team. We evaluate the overall energy cost of four projects, and we compare them to those of training the reported models. Our results show that the energy required for the development phase is 3 to 256 times greater than that required to train the best-performing model alone. These results advocate for a more systematic reporting of energy consumption across the entire life cycle of deep learning-based audio projects.

title: SupraTITO: Transferable Generative Molecular Dynamics for Supramolecular Systems
abstract: Peptide sequence governs both the structures formed through supramolecular assembly and the dynamics by which they emerge, but predicting either requires resolving slow collective processes among many interacting molecules. Molecular dynamics (MD) provides microscopic insight into these processes, yet the long timescales of assembly and the vast peptide sequence space make systematic exploration computationally demanding. We introduce SupraTITO, a transferable generative molecular dynamics (GenMD) framework for supramolecular systems, demonstrated through peptide self-assembly. SupraTITO learns transferable implicit transfer operators (TITO) conditioned on peptide sequence, molecular topology, and periodic geometry, allowing configurations to be propagated over physical intervals much longer than an MD integration step. On a comprehensive dipeptide benchmark, SupraTITO generalizes to held-out sequences and reproduces sequence-dependent structures and dynamics while maintaining molecular integrity over long rollouts. Compared with direct ensemble prediction trained on the same trajectory data, SupraTITO more accurately reproduces assembly structures while also resolving their temporal evolution. The learned dynamics generalize across peptide concentrations, including dilute conditions not represented during training. These results extend transferable GenMD to collective dynamics in periodic supramolecular systems and provide a foundation for modeling related processes beyond peptide assembly.

title: إمكانات توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي في تصميم استراتيجيات تعلم تكيفية لتعزيز الوعي بالأمن السيبراني: دراسة تحليلية
abstract: يهدف البحث إلى تحليل إمكانات توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي في تصميم استراتيجيات تعلم تكيفية لتعزيز الوعي بالأمن السيبراني، وتحديد الشروط التربوية والأمنية التي تحكم هذه الإمكانات. اعتمد البحث المنهج الوصفي التحليلي والتحليل النوعي للوثائق والبيانات الثانوية المنشورة، باستخدام مجموعة قصدية من عشر وثائق، منها تسع مؤرخة خلال 2023–2026 وصفحة حكومية غير مؤرخة، تشمل أربع دراسات علمية وأربعة أدلة وأطر دولية ومصدرين رسميين من السياق الإماراتي. استُخرج نوع الدليل وموضوعه وخصائص التكيف وضوابط الاستخدام وحدود الاستنتاج، مع التمييز بين اختبار الإمكان التقني وقياس التعلم المستقل والإرشاد المؤسسي، ولم تجمع الدراسة بيانات ميدانية أو تطبق برنامجًا تدريبيًا على طلبة. أظهر التحليل أن التوليد قد يتيح تنويع الأمثلة وتقديم تغذية راجعة وتعديل مستوى المساعدة، لكن مجرد إنتاج محتوى مختلف لا يكفي لاعتباره تعلمًا تكيفيًا. كما أن الدراسة المباشرة في التوعية السيبرانية اختبرت تسع شخصيات افتراضية، ولذلك تفيد في بيان الإمكان التقني دون إثبات تحسن سلوك متعلمين حقيقيين. وتبين الدراسات التعليمية المقارنة أن أثر المساعد يرتبط بتصميمه وطريقة قياس التعلم، ولا ينتقل تلقائيًا إلى الوعي السيبراني. وخلص البحث إلى إطار مقترح يربط الهدف الأمني بالتشخيص المحدود للمعرفة، والمحتوى المعتمد، وقواعد التكيف القابلة للتفسير، والمراجعة البشرية، والتقييم المستقل. ويوصي ببدء تطبيق تجريبي محدود بعد المراجعة المؤسسية، وقياس انتقال التعلم إلى مواقف جديدة، وتقليل البيانات المستخدمة في التخصيص، وعدم اتخاذ تقييم النموذج أساسًا منفردًا للقرارات الأكاديمية أو الأمنية.

title: Opere come dati: open data, diritto d’autore e patrimonio musicale alla prova dell’intelligenza artificiale generativa
abstract: Il contributo analizza l'intersezione tra le discipline europee sugli open data, il diritto d'autore e il patrimonio musicale alla luce dell'avvento dell'intelligenza artificiale generativa. Muovendo dalla duplice qualificazione che un medesimo oggetto culturale digitalizzato può assumere – come espressione protetta destinata alla fruizione estetica o come dato strutturato destinato al calcolo computazionale –, lo studio individua l'evoluzione del concetto di 'leggibilità meccanica' quale fattore chiave e ambivalente del quadro normativo. L'articolo propone la nozione concettuale di 'utilizzo informazionale' delle opere, distinto dalla fruizione tradizionale e dallo sfruttamento dell'espressione, ed evidenzia l'inadeguatezza del modello classico delle eccezioni e limitazioni dinanzi a tecnologie che richiedono un accesso sistemico all'intero corpus digitalizzato. Il patrimonio musicale e le istituzioni AFAM costituiscono il caso di studio ideale: il primo per l'estrema disaggregazione dei dati e frammentazione dei diritti, le seconde perché sintetizzano la natura di enti pubblici, custodi storici, centri di ricerca e produttori di nuove opere con IA.

Il patrimonio musicale e le istituzioni AFAM costituiscono il caso di studio ideale: il primo per l'estrema disaggregazione dei dati e frammentazione dei diritti, le seconde perché sintetizzano la natura di enti pubblici, custodi storici, centri di ricerca e produttori di nuove opere con IA.

title: Expanding cycles are not enough: a dichotomy for termination certificates of generalized Collatz maps
abstract: Preprint, Part I of two companion papers. Yolcu, Aaronson and Heule reduced the Collatz conjecture and several weakenings of it to the termination of string rewriting systems and proved some of them automatically. We explain this pattern for the positivity-preserving generalized Collatz maps that branch on residues modulo a power of 2 and apply affine branches (Ax+b)/2^e with A odd. If no strongly connected component of the finite abstraction graph on residues contains both an expanding cycle and a branching vertex (the map is disentangled), termination is decidable by a finite computation, and every terminating map has a staged valuation certificate: a lexicographic ranking function built from the logarithm, 2-adic valuations at finitely many rational periodic points, and finite-state weights. If some component contains both (the map is entangled), no such certificate exists, even with arbitrary bounded corrections: the obstruction is not an expanding cycle but its entanglement with branching. For entangled maps, including the Collatz map itself, no ranking function computed from the binary digits by positive, finite arctic, or primitive non-negative weighted automata of positive growth decreases at every step; the key is an equidistribution property of the binary digits of Terras preimages. The soundness of the certificates and five examples are checked in Lean 4; the code is on GitHub. Part II (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23081491) applies these results to the rewriting system itself. Prepared with substantial assistance from generative AI (Anthropic Claude); see the disclosure in the paper. Not yet reviewed by human experts.

title: Hybrid neuro-symbolic graph explanation framework for fraud detection in financial transaction networks
abstract: Introduction This research focuses on the development of a hybrid neuro-symbolic system for fraud detection in rapidly expanding digital financial systems. Methods A bipartite customer-merchant graph is constructed from the Nigerian Financial Transactions dataset, and a 3-layer Graph Attention Network (FraudGAT) is used to model structural dependencies while a symbolic reasoning layer and constrained LLM prompting generate auditor-readable explanations. Results On the curated evaluation split, FraudGAT achieves AUC 0.874, AUPRC 0.771, and F1 0.609. We additionally benchmark against GCN, GraphSAGE, GIN, a graphtransformer baseline, and tabular baselines (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM): tabular ensembles perform best on this sampled split, while FraudGAT remains stronger than several graph baselines and supports an interpretable detect-explain workflow. Discussions Therefore, we position the contribution as an auditable neuro-symbolic graph framework and an empirical foundation for scaling to larger, richer transaction graphs.

title: Aviation Crash Predictor Using Multi-Dimensional Self-Explainable Modern Machine Learning Approach and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)
abstract: : This study presents a machine learning algorithm designed to forecast potential causes of a new aircraft crash based on a previously learned dataset. The primary objective of this research is to minimize the time and expenses incurred by both the investigator and the aviation sector's investigation department. A significant amount of time is expended by aviation investigators to ascertain or hypothesize the actual cause of aircraft crashes. We have utilized tools such as VS Code, Python, Hugging Face, scikit-learn, and SHAP for this research to develop the model, test the models, and implement the explainer. In this study, we initially identify the optimal dataset by refining and tuning the structure of the dataset. Subsequently, we preprocessed the dataset using multiple processing tools like vectorizer and encoder to make the dataset suitable for model training. To achieve maximum accuracy from the model, we go for a multiple model approach where we divide the dataset into two parts. In the initial section, we consolidate all minor classes into a single overarching class, whereas in the subsequent segment, we focus exclusively on minor classes and exclude all major classes. Besides, we train several models like XGBoost, Random Forest, and Decision Tree on each segment to find the best possible optimal model by analyzing the outcomes from each model on each segment. In the selected model, we employed Explainable AI to improve interpretability by illustrating the contribution of individual features to the selected predictions. We have finalized two models that achieve remarkable accuracies of 96% and 98%, respectively, in the major and minor class segments. The recall values, along with the F1 score, are attaining commendable results of approximately 90%. In terms of explainability, the model assigns optimal and maximal weights to the features that are directly responsible for the specific outcome.

title: Comparison of Integrated Versus Sequential Artificial Intelligence–Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis Systems in Breast Ultrasound: A Prospective Pilot Study on Examination Time, Reproducibility, and Diagnostic Performance
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To compare integrated and sequential artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis (AI-CAD) systems in terms of examination time, reproducibility, and diagnostic performance in breast ultrasound (US). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective single-center study included women who underwent breast US at a breast imaging center between February and March 2025. Two real-time AI-CAD systems were evaluated: an integrated system providing simultaneous lesion detection and diagnosis during scanning, and a sequential system in which lesion detection and diagnostic assessment were performed separately. Examination time was assessed in patients who underwent paired breast US examinations with both AI-CAD systems during the same visit, with randomized examination order. Reproducibility was assessed by applying both systems twice to the same breast lesions. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: Examination time analysis included 97 patients and showed longer examination time with sequential AI-CAD than with integrated AI-CAD (P < .001), regardless of examination order. Reproducibility analysis included 145 patients with 215 lesions and showed almost perfect agreement between the first and second acquisitions for both systems (integrated vs. sequential: κ = 0.81 vs. 0.83). For the comparison between the first and second acquisitions, κ values for the integrated versus sequential systems were 0.92 versus 0.76 for malignant lesions, 0.79 versus 0.84 for mass lesions, and 1.00 versus 0.75 for nonmass lesions. However, agreement patterns varied across other scan-plane comparisons. Diagnostic performance analysis included 242 patients. Integrated AI-CAD showed higher sensitivity (integrated vs. sequential: 87.6% vs. 76.9%; P < .001), whereas sequential AI-CAD showed higher specificity (integrated vs. sequential: 74.2% vs. 90.0%; P < .001). AUC did not differ between the two systems. CONCLUSION: Integrated and sequential AI-CAD systems showed complementary strengths in breast US. Integrated AI-CAD favored shorter examination time and higher sensitivity, whereas sequential AI-CAD favored higher specificity, with reproducibility differing according to lesion type.

title: Updatable Timed‐Release Conditional Broadcast Proxy Re‐Encryption Scheme for CAMIN
abstract: ABSTRACT In cloud‐assisted medical information networks (CAMIN), patients often store their sensitive data in encrypted form on the cloud. This data needs to be shared with doctors to enable efficient medical services, while also ensuring the protection of patient privacy. Therefore, data sharing and privacy protection have become critical challenges. Proxy re‐encryption has been widely studied as an important technique for ciphertext sharing; most existing schemes still suffer from several limitations: first, they usually lack constraints on decryption time, allowing the recipient to decrypt the re‐encrypted ciphertext immediately upon receipt; second, most existing schemes don't impose restrictions on the re‐encryption capability of the cloud server, leading to abuse of re‐encryption privileges; third, many schemes rely on expensive cryptographic operations, resulting in high computational and communication overheads. To address these issues, an updatable timed‐release conditional broadcast proxy re‐encryption scheme is proposed. This scheme embeds access conditions and a time‐lock mechanism into the re‐encryption key, ensuring that ciphertext transformation can only occur when specified conditions are met. Furthermore, decryption is restricted to be executed only when the designated time arrives. Security analysis shows our scheme provides indistinguishability against chosen ciphertext attacks in the random oracle model and remains secure against collusion attacks. Performance evaluation indicates significant advantages in both computational and communication costs, making this scheme highly suitable for data sharing in CAMIN.

title: Halving the cost of QROM again via dense encoding
abstract: Quantum read only memory (QROM) is a substantial source of non-Clifford cost in fault-tolerant quantum algorithms. Borrowing dirty qubits can reduce this cost, provided their unknown initial states are restored. We consider the practically relevant qubit-constrained regime, where limited workspace restricts the table-block size and table loading dominates the cost. For $N$ entries of $b$ bits and approximately $bλ$ dirty qubits, SelectSwap has leading Toffoli count $2N/λ$. Recent work using sequential bit packets reduces this to $(1+1/b)N/λ$. In this work we introduce a dense encoding construction of QROM, where two bits of classical information are stored in each dirty qubit instead of one by utilizing both the $Z$ and $X$ bases. On its own, dense encoding provides a $2\times$ improvement over SelectSwap by reducing the leading Toffoli count to $N/λ$. Combining it with sequential bit packets gives $\tfrac12(1+1/b)N/λ$, a further halving of the sequential construction's leading cost, and an approximately $4\times$ improvement over SelectSwap in the large-$N$ limit for practical values of $b$.

title: Where LLMs Fail with Visualization DSLs
abstract: As LLMs take up the role of authoring charts using visualization domain-specific languages (DSLs), the human constraints that shaped those languages may no longer apply, as what is easy for a person is not necessarily easy for a model. To understand how LLMs might work better with DSLs, we explore where and how they fail with current DSL designs. We evaluate 10 JSON-style visualization DSLs with 41 tasks across 3 LLMs, then assess the generated specifications with JSON and rendering checks, and qualitative coding of failed cases. Analyzing how this specification generation process fails, we identify four recurring failure patterns, link each to specific DSL features, and discuss design considerations for future DSL designs.

title: Generation Provenance Before Behavior Attribution: Auditing Synthetic Speech Research Objects
abstract: Attributing model behavior to synthetic training data requires knowing what produced each training item before estimating what that item caused. A waveform-label pair does not preserve this knowledge. We propose a generation-provenance substrate in which a synthetic research object binds source specification, generated content, waveform, target, fact requirements, quality signals, review lineage, and immutable manifest identity. Producer and selection mechanism determine evidentiary meaning; storage location and variable name do not. We audit this substrate in a private Japanese care-handoff pipeline. A 113-asset review population contains 1.552 hours of synthetic speech across six scenario families; all items have linked audio, transcripts, candidate notes, and fact checklists, but human evidence is selective and source-specific. Two faithful-only manifests are scenario-seed-disjoint and immutably versioned, while exact upstream attribution remains blocked by floating generator aliases, missing per-clip TTS and code stamps, and an unversioned checking prompt. We argue that generation provenance is necessary but not sufficient for behavior attribution: it defines the candidate causal graph and audit units, whereas contributive attribution still requires frozen training runs and intervention or influence evidence. The paper contributes a compact provenance contract, an audit protocol, and a bounded case study for synthetic-data attribution; controlled research access may be offered, but we do not claim causal training-data attribution, clinical validity, or unrestricted public release.

title: Experience-Based Feasibility-Aware Generative Adversarial Imitation from Observation under Embodiment Mismatch
abstract: With the increasing use of robot-free demonstration interfaces that provide state trajectories without action labels, imitation from observation has become a promising approach for learning robot behaviors from human demonstrations. However, due to differences in embodiment and dynamics between humans and robots, demonstrated human motions may not be feasible for the robot, potentially degrading policy performance. In this study, we propose Experience-Based Feasibility-Aware Generative Adversarial Imitation from Observation (EF-GAIfO), which estimates the feasibility of state-only demonstrations from the robot's own experience rather than relying on explicit dynamics models or large prior exploration datasets. A key feature of EF-GAIfO is that the notion of feasibility evolves with policy learning: as the policy improves and the robot experiences a broader range of state transitions, the feasible region is progressively expanded, allowing additional demonstrations to be incorporated into learning. This enables feasibility-aware imitation that adapts to the current stage of policy learning, rather than relying on a pre-designed feasibility criterion. We validate the effectiveness of EF-GAIfO on a locomotion task in simulation and on a real quadruped robot performing a object-reaching-and-grasping task.

title: Sublinear-depth Quantum Simulation of Electrons with Atomic Orbitals
abstract: Discretizing electronic degrees of freedom into atomic orbitals is the default choice to accurately model electrons in molecules in a compact and flexible way. We consider the task of simulating such electronic structure models on a quantum computer for $N$ orbitals, keeping the number of orbitals per atom constant. Atomic orbitals give rise to Hamiltonians with potentially up to $\mathcal{O}(N^4)$ terms and little structure, which made it challenging to match the complexity of methods based on plane waves and real-space grids. In this work, we show that a Trotter step for atomic orbitals can be implemented in depth $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{polylog}(N))$ without ancillas by combining a rigorous treatment of orbital localization, a hierarchical Hamiltonian decomposition based on the Fast Multipole Method, and shallow quantum Fourier arithmetic circuits. By bounding the Trotter error, we obtain sublinear simulation depth, and our total gate count $N^{5/3 + o(1)}$ matches the best scaling known for any basis.

title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Hydrological Models
abstract: Abstract The evaluation of hydrological models is essential for both model selection and reliability assessment. However, comparing predictions with observations alone is insufficient to fully characterize model behavior. This limitation is particularly relevant to deep learning (DL) models because of their complex internal structures. In risk‐averse operational settings, water managers require models whose reliability and failure modes have been carefully evaluated because unstable predictions can put critical infrastructure at risk. Motivated by the need to assess model reliability before operational deployment, we introduce and explore adversarial robustness analysis for hydrological modeling and evaluate whether small, targeted perturbations to meteorological forcings induce substantial changes in simulated discharge. We compare a physical‐conceptual model (HBV) with a deep learning‐based model (LSTM) across 1,347 German catchments using perturbations of varying magnitudes generated by the fast gradient sign method (FGSM). We find that FGSM perturbations generally reduce Kling–Gupta efficiency and increase mean squared error. However, widespread catastrophic failures under the specific FGSM perturbations are not observed, and LSTM generally exhibits less performance degradation than HBV. In the examined catchments, changes in the predicted hydrographs and time‐averaged internal model states often vary approximately linearly with perturbation magnitude, providing a compact summary of how errors grow under such perturbations. evidence.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Hydrological Models
evidence.abstract: Abstract The evaluation of hydrological models is essential for both model selection and reliability assessment. However, comparing predictions with observations alone is insufficient to fully characterize model behavior. This limitation is particularly relevant to deep learning (DL) models because of their complex internal structures. In risk‐averse operational settings, water managers require models whose reliability and failure modes have been carefully evaluated because unstable predictions can put critical infrastructure at risk. Motivated by the need to assess model reliability before operational deployment, we introduce and explore adversarial robustness analysis for hydrological modeling and evaluate whether small, targeted perturbations to meteorological forcings induce substantial changes in simulated discharge. We compare a physical‐conceptual model (HBV) with a deep learning‐based model (LSTM) across 1,347 German catchments using perturbations of varying magnitudes generated by the fast gradient sign method (FGSM). We find that FGSM perturbations generally reduce Kling–Gupta efficiency and increase mean squared error. However, widespread catastrophic failures under the specific FGSM perturbations are not observed, and LSTM generally exhibits less performance degradation than HBV. In the examined catchments, changes in the predicted hydrographs and time‐averaged internal model states often vary approximately linearly with perturbation magnitude, providing a compact summary of how errors grow under such perturbations. Similar patterns are observed along random perturbation directions in selected catchments, suggesting that, in those catchments, small input changes produce approximately proportional changes in model output. Overall, these findings characterize local predictive stability under controlled stress tests and motivate future studies of model robustness in real‐world operational settings.

title: Intelligenza artificiale e proprietà intellettuale – Tra sfide legali e innovazione digitale
abstract: Il rapido sviluppo dell'intelligenza artificiale sta ridefinendo i confini del diritto della proprietà intellettuale, mettendo in discussione il tradizionale concetto antropocentrico di autore. L'articolo analizza l'impatto dell'IA sulle categorie classiche del diritto d'autore, esaminando il quadro normativo europeo — dal Regolamento AI Act 2024/1689 alla Direttiva Copyright 2019/790/UE — e le recenti iniziative legislative italiane, tra cui il DDL n. 1146, oggi convertito nella legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132. Attraverso l'analisi del concetto giurisprudenziale di plagio evolutivo e lo studio di casi emblematici (Thaler v. USPTO e il robot artista Ai-Da), il contributo riflette sulla necessità di un ripensamento delle nozioni di autorialità e creatività nell'era digitale, prospettando un equilibrio tra innovazione tecnologica e tutela dei diritti degli autori.

title: VitalDB IOH threshold expansion and monitoring-source dependence: analysis code
abstract: Version 1.0.0 analysis code for a retrospective methodological cohort study using VitalDB, examining MAP-threshold expansion, monitoring-source dependence and incremental prediction of postoperative ICU utilisation. Contains Python source, synthetic tests, retrospective input-byte fingerprints and 12 aggregate reference tables. No raw clinical data, patient-level derivatives or predictions are included. Inputs must be obtained separately from official VitalDB sources under their own terms. Staged local revalidation rebuilt exposures and reran 12 models using five patient-grouped cross-validation repeats and 2,000 bootstrap replicates, matching all supplied aggregate reference tables. Bootstrap conditions on fixed out-of-fold predictions without model refitting. Not a clinical decision tool or external validation. MIT applies ONLY to original Python source and synthetic tests, NOT upstream data, input fingerprints, manuscript text or aggregate tables. title: RIA-ViT: A Residual Inception Atrous Vision Transformer for Detection of Gallbladder Cancer from CT Images
abstract: Gallbladder Cancer (GBC) is a rare but highly aggressive malignancy of the biliary system. In early-stage gallbladder cancer, there are neither overt symptoms nor specific signs. In most patients, it is diagnosed late, resulting in poor outcomes. Even when imaging is available, diagnosing GBC remains difficult because its features overlap with those of non-neoplastic gallbladder pathologies. Furthermore, the overlap between GBC features and those of benign gallbladder conditions may require expert radiological interpretation, which is sometimes unavailable in developing countries. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to design and develop a CT-based framework for automated gallbladder cancer detection that is clinically interpretable, enabling early, consistent, and reliable detection to mitigate diagnostic variability and assist clinicians in making informed decisions. The framework incorporates a hybrid deep learning model, the Residual Inception Atrous Vision Transformer (RIA-ViT), which uses convolutional neural networks to extract local features and vision transformers to contextualize global features. The innovative design incorporates inception residual blocks for multi-scale learning, atrous convolution for enlarging the receptive field, and separable convolution for efficient design. The features are embedded and processed using transformer encoders. The proposed framework was evaluated on a well-curated dataset of CT images of GBC and normal cases, achieving an average classification accuracy of 99.56%. The model accurately separated GBC CT images from normal gallbladder CT images. The proposed framework offers reliable diagnostic outcomes with interpretable, trustworthy visual evidence. The RIA-ViT framework is a major advancement towards the development of automated systems for GBC from CT images.

title: DWR-CvT with Vanilla GAN-Based Synthetic Data Generation for Cervical Cancer Classification
abstract: Cervical cancer is a major cause of mortality among women worldwide, making early and accurate diagnosis essential. This study proposes Vanilla GAN-based data augmentation combined with a Depthwise Separable Convolution and Residual-based Convolutional Vision Transformer (DWR-CvT) for cervical cell classification. DWR-CvT integrates Depthwise Separable Convolution (DSC) and Residual Connection (RC) before the transformer block to enhance feature extraction while maintaining computational efficiency. The study conducted two experimental setups, including 5-class and 7-class classification tasks, and validated the approach on an external dataset, SIPaKMeD, to evaluate generalization. Cervical cell images were generated using Vanilla GAN, achieving FID 32, LPIPS 0.36, and Cosine Similarity 0.812. The augmented datasets were used to train the proposed DWR-CvT model. Experimental results show 97% accuracy, 96–97% sensitivity, 97–99% specificity, 97–98% precision, 97% F1-score, and 99% AUC across all experiments. The model contains only 0.53 million parameters, indicating greater computational efficiency than conventional deep learning architectures. These findings demonstrate that integrating Vanilla GAN augmentation with the DWR-CvT provides an effective, lightweight, and robust solution for cervical cancer cell classification across multiple class granularities and datasets. The proposed method achieves consistent performance while reducing computational cost, making it suitable for practical clinical and research applications.

title: Semi-declarative Language for Combinatorial Search
abstract: Combinatorial search—finding solutions that meet constraints within an exponentially large space of candidates—underpins problems from hardware verification to scheduling and combinatorial design. The most successful approach in practice is Propositional Satisfiability (SAT) solving, but modelling a problem for a SAT solver requires manually translating high-level requirements into conjunctions of boolean clauses, a tedious step that sacrifices clarity and modularity. Answer Set Programming (ASP) offers a higher-level alternative, with a rule-based language whose variables and finite-domain reasoning yield more compact problem descriptions that can be automatically compiled into low-level solver input. Yet, ASP has its own shortcomings: its semantics, defined via a notion of stable models, is hard to build intuition for; it does not allow arbitrary first-order logic formulas as constraints; and its programs tend to be monolithic, making modular design and reuse difficult. We propose SetLah!, a semi-declarative language for combinatorial search that addresses the shortcomings of both SAT and ASP. A SetLah! program is a sequence of stratified blocks, each containing rules that define the search space and arbitrary first-order logic constraints that prune it. This block structure enables modular problem decomposition, allowing for an intuitive semantics: candidate solutions are generated and filtered block by block. We built a compiler from SetLah! programs into ASP, allowing us to take full advantage of the existing efficient ASP solvers, while also automatically optimising the generated encodings. Our empirical evaluation demonstrates that SetLah! offers substantially more concise and intuitive specifications for common combinatorial search problems, and its compiled ASP encodings can significantly outperform SAT-based tools.

title: An improved isolation forest based on kernel principal component analysis for anomaly detection in helicopter-based power-line inspection data
abstract: For helicopter inspection data, including flight trajectories, task status, and equipment operating status, conventional anomaly detection methods still suffer from difficulties in separating high-dimensional nonlinear data, insufficient anomaly isolation capability, and low anomaly discrimination. To address these problems, this paper proposes an improved isolation forest anomaly detection method based on kernel principal component analysis (KPCA). The proposed method extracts five categories of features from inspection data, including standard deviation, coefficient of variation, centroid, resilience, and scale features, and constructs a fused feature matrix through sliding windows. KPCA is then used to perform nonlinear reconstruction and dimensionality reduction on the feature matrix to obtain a low-dimensional subspace. In this subspace, the single axis-aligned splitting strategy of the conventional isolation forest is improved into multi-directional splitting along principal-component directions and their combined directions. In addition, the path length is corrected according to the distance between each sample and the normal center .Experimental results based on 7027 real records from a helicopter inspection platform show that the proposed method outperforms conventional methods in terms of Precision, Recall, F1-score, FAR, and PR-AUC. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively identify flight-trajectory deviations, equipment operation anomalies, and task-execution anomalies, providing a feasible data-driven technical approach for improving the intelligence and reliability of power-line inspection.

title: From Network Intrusion Detection to Blockchain-Backed Endpoint Detection and Response: Mapping the Landscape of Decentralized Detection-and-Response Architectures
abstract: While the literature on blockchain-assisted intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS) for Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks is mature, existing systematic reviews suffer from two critical limitations: they overlook the structural shift toward modern Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) and Extended Detection and Response (XDR) architectures, and they conflate blockchain's distinct functional roles into a single monolithic category. This Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) addresses these gaps by proposing a three-axis taxonomy that classifies proposals by detection-system class (NIDS, HIDS, EDR/XDR), blockchain functional role, and response-automation maturity. Synthesizing research published in high-impact venues between 2019 and 2026, we provide a rigorous gap analysis exposing why a genuine per-endpoint blockchain-anchored response loop remains nearly nonexistent due to latency, deployment, and community mismatches. Furthermore, we evaluate structural, cross-cutting challenges persisting across the literature, including consensus latency on constrained devices, post-quantum cryptographic vulnerability, smart-contract attack surfaces, and the adversarial vulnerability of evolving LLM-based detection engines. Finally, we outline a comprehensive research agenda centered on hybrid on-chain/off-chain orchestration to bridge the gap between decentralized trust and rapid response automation.

title: Can LLMs Reliably Annotate Bioassay Metadata to Improve Data Readiness?
abstract: The emergence of foundation models for molecular property prediction requires a high degree of AI data readiness, including reliable metadata annotation. However, both public repositories and industrial screening databases suffer from missing, inconsistent, or conflated assay annotations. In this work, we quantify the extent of missing annotations in PubChem for the BioAssay Ontology (BAO) assay format and physical detection method fields and investigate whether open-source and proprietary large language models (LLMs) can reliably predict and audit metadata annotations directly from the assay text. In our assessment, we found that the annotation coverage across PubChem's $\sim$2 million bioassays is critically sparse, 36\% lacking an assay format, 89\% a BioAssay type, and >99.9\% any BAO-mapped assay format or detection technology term. This motivates the need for automated test-metadata curation. Using evaluation sets derived from PubChem and ChEMBL, we assess the agreement of seven open-source and proprietary LLMs with existing silver labels. Recall is at least 0.96 for biochemical and cell-based assay formats, with a similar pattern for detection technology, although disagreements increase on under-represented classes. Manual inspection shows that many of these disagreements trace back to inconsistencies between silver sources rather than to LLM error. Moreover, in a qualitative study with a senior industrial curator, LLM-generated evidence prompted the expert to revise some of their own labels, showing LLMs can flag potentially mislabeled assays. Across the study, performance differences between proprietary and open-source models were small. Together, these results suggest LLMs can support the large-scale annotation and auditing of assay metadata, though per-class reliability estimates and targeted human review remain necessary before such labels enter downstream ML pipelines.

title: Electromagnetic drift-kinetic particle-in-cell model with energy and charge conservation for studying finite-β plasmas
abstract: The paper proposes a generalization of the fully implicit energy- and charge-conserving electromagnetic particle-in-cell method to the case where the lightest type of plasma particle (electrons) is described in the drift-kinetic approximation. This allows us to remove the very strict time step limitation of this method requiring to resolve the gyrorotation of electrons. Since the drift-kinetic model is only applicable to light particles whose contribution to plasma polarization is small, this model can be further simplified by neglecting the electron polarization drift and including in Maxwell's equations, in addition to the current of gyrocenters, only the magnetization current. In order for such a hybrid model to retain conservative properties in finite-difference form, a method of self-consistent interpolation of nabla B in the mirror force from grid to particle and the magnetization vector from particle to grid is proposed. Unlike existing drift-kinetic models, this model is not limited to considering small perturbations near a given equilibrium, and therefore allows one to study the formation of plasma equilibria in regimes with a finite ratio of plasma to magnetic field pressure. Testing of the parallel code implemented in C++ using the PETSc library confirmed the fulfillment of the finite-difference laws of energy and charge conservation, as well as the ability of the model (in the drift-kinetic version for all types of particles) to correctly reproduce the diamagnetic effect and longitudinal ion-acoustic wave.

title: Research on privacy protection strategies for multi-sensor data in smart museum interactive display systems
abstract: To address the core challenge of synergistically optimizing privacy protection, data utility, system real-time performance, and privacy budget utilization efficiency in multi-sensor interaction scenarios of smart museums, this paper proposes a hierarchical adaptive privacy protection strategy that integrates local differential privacy and federated learning (abbreviated as: LDP-FL-HAPPS). This method employs a multi-sensor data hierarchical model to classify collected data into core privacy-level and general privacy-level categories, achieving differentiated privacy protection. A dynamic LDP perturbation mechanism is used to adjust noise intensity in real time based on data sensitivity, minimizing data distortion while ensuring privacy. A privacy-aware federated fusion algorithm is designed to optimize the accuracy and transmission efficiency of multi-sensor data fusion, which can enhance data visualization effectiveness. A hierarchical adaptive budget al.location strategy is introduced, combining data privacy levels with feature correlation to achieve efficient utilization and rational allocation of the privacy budget. Experimental results demonstrate that the hierarchical privacy budget al.location strategy proposed in this paper is highly effective in protecting multi-sensor data privacy. Under various privacy budget configurations, the system’s overall privacy leakage probability can be as low as 4.5%. In an extreme scenario involving 1,000 membership inference attacks, the leakage probability for core privacy-sensitive data was only 8.9%, it validates the method’s effectiveness in defending against adaptive attacks. With a mean squared error (MSE) of 0.334, a total data processing latency of approximately 68 ms, and a privacy budget utilization rate reaching 95.7%, this approach offers an efficient and reliable technical solution for multi-sensor privacy protection in smart museums.

title: Interface Architectures for Low-Latency Cryogenic Control in Quantum-Classical Systems
abstract: As superconducting and silicon-spin quantum processors scale from hundreds to thousands of physical qubits, the interconnect bottleneck between room-temperature classical electronics and mK cryogenic quantum processors poses a critical physical and architectural barrier. Low-latency control loops—essential for Quantum Error Correction (QED), fast reset protocols, and adaptive quantum algorithms—are strictly constrained by thermal load budgets, speed-of-light signal latency across thermal stages, and the bandwidth limits of coax lines. This paper presents a detailed architectural framework for next-generation quantum-classical interfaces. We investigate the transition from traditional, room-temperature arbitrary waveform generators (AWGs) connected via coaxial lines to co-integrated, cryo-CMOS, and single-flux-quantum (SFQ) digital-to-analog and digital signal processing control layers operating directly at the 4 K and 20 mK stages. We evaluate thermal transport, power dissipation, signal attenuation, and physical routing constraints, proposing a heterogeneous hybrid-control topology that satisfies latency budgets below 100 ns while remaining within the tight thermal limits of modern dilution refrigerators.

title: Bounded Kan Composition, Clifford Stalk Closures, and Invariant-Driven Cell Rewriting in Topological and Geometric Native Coding for Higher Dimensional Programming Languages
abstract: For over seven decades, computer architecture has operated under a single, unstated dogma: that physical space, continuous motion, field mechanics, and multi-agent coordination must be forcibly flattened into the unoriented, one-dimensional byte array of the von Neumann machine. While this linear abstraction democratized software engineering, it severed computation from the native geometry and topology of the physical universe, imposing artificial concurrency locks, memory wall thrashing, and empirical termination heuristics upon spatial problems. Topological and Geometric Native Coding fundamentally reframes the nature of computation. Rather than executing sequences of instructions against passive, flat memory, execution proceeds directly over graded, cell-oriented topological complexes governed by the fundamental discrete boundary law: $$\partial \circ \partial = 0$$ In this paradigm, state is distributed across multi-dimensional cells (points, lines, surfaces, volumes, hypercells) carrying coordinate-free geometric fibers belonging to a Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}(p,q,r)$. Control flow is not driven by arbitrary counter loops or boolean flags; it is driven by topological invariants. Execution iterates until spatial obstructions and non-contractible voids collapse, quantified by the kernel nullity of a discrete combinatorial Hodge Laplacian: $$L_k = B_k^\top B_k + B_{k+1} B_{k+1}^\top, \qquad \beta_k = \dim(\ker(L_k))$$ This repository contains the complete theoretical foundation, intermediate representation (MLIR dialect), formal verification suite (Lean 4), C-ABI specifications, and bare-metal execution runtime for ToposLang-Cubical—the compiler architecture that resolves the fundamental execution bottleneck of higher-dimensional programming languages. The Core Duality: Solving the Homotopy Scalability Dilemma ToposLang-Cubical operationalizes a profound structural duality long recognized in pure category theory but hitherto unexploited in systems engineering: discrete homological algebra and continuous constructive homotopy are not competing paradigms, but multi-scale expressions of the same underlying geometric reality. Prior to this work, implementations of topological computing faced an unyielding trade-off: The Global Rational Integer Explosion Problem ($\mathbb{Q}$-RREF): Standard discrete cell complexes evaluate exact invariants via Gaussian elimination on boundary matrices. Over rational fields ($\mathbb{Q}$), row pivot cross-multiplication induces Hadamard determinant growth, causing intermediate numerators and denominators to explode past thousands of bits ($O(n^3)$ operations). Execution throughput degrades by four orders of magnitude, saturating memory bandwidth. The Unbounded Kan Memory Problem (Cubical Type Theory): Constructive Cubical Type Theory (CTT) synthesizes continuous homotopies dynamically on-demand via Kan filling operations (hcomp). However, in higher dimensions, resolving boundary coherences generates infinite towers of higher homotopies ($\pi_1 \Rightarrow \pi_2 \Rightarrow \dots \Rightarrow \pi_\infty$). Allocated on dynamic heaps, these towers exhaust physical RAM and lack the global spatial routing required for local updates. The ToposLang-Cubical Solution: Global macro-spatial structure is governed by sparse integer boundary operators on physical memory. Whenever a localized topological obstruction arises ($L_k c \neq 0$), a Three-Tier Topological Trigger Engine extracts its minimal downward support and lowers it via a formal Realization Functor ($\mathcal{R}$) into a local, stack-allocated, $n$-truncated Kan composition engine. By evaluating continuous Lie group motor sandwiches ($PGA(3,0,1)$) inside zero-heap, cache-aligned 192-byte C-ABI stack frames (KanStackFrame), the runtime synthesizes terminal filling cells in $O(1)$ stack memory, completely bypassing global rational matrix inversion. Architectural & Theoretical Breakthroughs The Formal Realization Functor ($\mathcal{R}$): Mathematically bridges discrete chain complexes with constructive cubical sets: $$\mathcal{R} : \mathrm{Chain}_{\mathrm{Cl}(p,q,r)}(U) \longrightarrow \mathrm{CubSet}_{/X}$$ Compiles sparse boundary columns $(B_k)_{*j}$ into bitwise boolean face constraint masks $\varphi \in \mathrm{Face}(I^{k+1})$ without loss of algebraic orientation. Three-Tier Topological Trigger Engine: Eliminates the $O(n^3)$ cycle-detection loop bottleneck during invariant evaluation (until betti(k) == 0): Tier 1 ($O(1)$ Fast Path): Local support patching tracks boundary changes in $<50\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. Tier 2 ($O(\alpha(N))$ Filter): Lock-free Union-Find connectivity checks suppress $>77\%$ of false-alarm trigger checks. Tier 3 ($\mathbb{Z}_p$ Finite-Field Reduction): Sparse elimination over prime field $\mathbb{Z}_p$ ($p = 10007$) calculates exact homology ranks in fixed 64-bit machine integers, resolving macro Betti jumps in $\sim 1.6\text{ ms}$. Dual Cache-Aligned C-ABI (KanStackFrame): A strict 64-byte aligned, 192-byte C-compatible thread structure (3 cache lines) featuring a 64-bit face constraint mask (uint64_t) supporting complex polyhedral cells with up to 32 boundary faces ($k \le 31$) with zero heap allocation. Lie Manifold Projection Operator ($\pi_{\PGA}$): In-line projection ($\hat{r} = r/\Vert{}r\Vert{}$) during continuous Projective Geometric Algebra ($\mathrm{PGA}(3,0,1)$) versor sandwich evaluations ($u(t) = M(t) u_0 \widetilde{M}(t)$), holding floating-point norm drift to exact machine precision ($0.00 \times 10^0$) over $50{,}000+$ consecutive transformation steps. The topos_cubical MLIR Dialect: Lowering infrastructure providing native operations for Kan box extraction (bridge_lower), stack composition (hcomp), and dynamic degree pruning (truncate). Lock-Free Spatial Concurrency: Spatially disjoint wavefronts ($\mathrm{supp}(r_1) \cap \mathrm{supp}(r_2) = \varnothing$) enable parallel cellular rewriting with zero lock contention and zero cache invalidation across 128 physical cores. Empirical Benchmark Performance Evaluated on a dual-socket workstation equipped with two AMD EPYC 7763 processors (128 physical cores, 256 logical threads, 256 MB L3 cache per socket), 512 GB DDR4 ECC RAM, running Linux kernel 6.8: Metric / Scenario Classical $\mathbb{Q}$-RREF ToposLang-Cubical Bridge Performance Gain Cycle Resolution Latency ($N = 4,096$ edges) 4,112.5 ms 0.152 ms 27,055.9$\times$ Speedup Max Intermediate Bit-Length 8,192 bits Fixed 64-bit / Double Zero Bit-Length Growth Execution Memory Footprint Dynamic Heap ($O(n^3)$) 192 Bytes Stack ($O(1)$) Bounded Memory Invariant Parallel Rewrite Throughput (128 Cores) Unscalable (Lock Bottlenecks) 72,100 Rules / sec 87.9$\times$ Scaling Efficiency

title: Prompt Injection Under the Invariant Taxonomy: Failure-Mode Analysis and Proof of Hallucination-Independent State Conservation
abstract: Document Reference: ARC-ANL-INJ-002Companion Specification: ARC-SPEC-AGENT-HCE-001 (10.5281/zenodo.23076445)Governing Framework: Invariant Taxonomy (Physical, Digital, Legacy)Primary Invariant Proved: Theorem 1 (State Conservation Under DENY: D(a) = DENY ⇒ Δ_external = 0)Target Master Anchor: A-77-DELTA-SHIELD-LOCKED (10.5281/zenodo.22665852) This paper presents a formal failure-mode trace and mathematical proof demonstrating that runtime prompt injection attacks against non-deterministic AI producers yield non-zero state mutation (Δ_external ≠ 0) under Legacy Invariants with probability P → 1 as attempts increase, but guarantee zero external state mutation (Δ_external = 0) under Digital Invariants for every DENY verdict, regardless of model context, hallucination, or injection depth. Key Contributions:- Legacy Failure-Mode Trace: Demonstrates that intent classifiers with positive false-negative rates (p > 0) decay asymptotically under repeated injection variants (P_bypass = 1 - (1-p)^N → 1).- Digital Invariant Trace: Traces four malicious injection actions (overpressure, alarm suppression, socket exfiltration, bpf map tampering) through Rust gate envelope predicates and eBPF LSM hooks.- Formal Proof of State Conservation: Establishes Lemma 1 (Egress Isolation), Lemma 2 (Non-Interference), Lemma 3 (Single-Use Tokens), and Theorem 1 (State Conservation Under DENY).- Constant Residual Risk Corollary: Proves that residual bypass probability under Digital Invariants equals TCB failure probability and is strictly constant in adversary attempts N.

title: Adaptive Graph Sparsification for Efficient Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This preprint presents an experimental study of graph sparsification for graph neural networks. The study evaluates multiple edge-selection strategies, including random, degree-based, structural, feature-based, and multi-criteria sparsification, across the Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed, Chameleon, and Squirrel datasets. The experiments examine the relationship between edge retention and predictive performance using test accuracy and macro-F1, together with training and computational time. Pairwise ablation experiments further evaluate the contributions of structural similarity, node-feature similarity, and local connectivity components within the proposed multi-criteria framework. The study also analyzes graph characteristics and computational performance across datasets with different structural and homophily properties. Results are reported across multiple retention ratios and random seeds. The uploaded document contains the research methodology, experimental results, ablation analysis, discussion, limitations, and references.

title: LLM-Enhanced Bayesian Knowledge Tracing for Continuous Performance Modeling and Adaptive Programming Learning
abstract: Accurate estimation of learners’ skill mastery is essential for adaptive learning systems, particularly in programming education, where evaluating learner performance remains challenging due to the complexity of code assessment and the need to capture partial correctness and diverse learning behaviors. This study aims to improve mastery estimation and adaptive exercise recommendations through a continuous knowledge-tracing approach based on an extension of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing. The proposed approach integrates continuous performance scores from an automated evaluation process that combines structural code analysis, dynamic testing, and large language model–based analysis, while accounting for task difficulty and guidance format. The estimated mastery is then used to recommend programming exercises adapted to the learner’s knowledge state. To evaluate the approach, controlled simulations involving diverse learner profiles and real interaction data were conducted. Results show that the proposed model variants reduce mastery estimation error by up to 70% compared with the baseline model, particularly for learners with low and average proficiency levels. Furthermore, the approach improves estimation stability and generates recommendations consistent with learner progression. The main contribution of this work is a continuous extension of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing that leverages fine-grained assessment data to improve learner modeling and adaptive exercise recommendation in programming education.

title: Explainable AI for malware opcode sequence analysis and explainability-motivated saliency-map based spurious correlation robustness in images
abstract: Explainability offers a powerful lens for understanding and improving the robustness of Machine Learning (ML) models. This work demonstrates how eXplainable AI (XAI) techniques can be used not only to interpret model behaviour, but also to develop robust training algorithms that encourage the learning of semantically meaningful features. The first contribution is Hierarchical-LIME (H-LIME), a novel XAI method tailored to malicious Android opcode sequence analysis. Unlike standard LIME, which treats individual opcodes as flat, independent features, H-LIME leverages the hierarchical structure of programs, such as classes and methods, to produce sparser and more descriptively accurate explanations, improving the localisation of malicious code segments. The second contribution, UnLearning from Experience (ULE), integrates explainability into the training process of image classifiers by leveraging saliency maps to guide model behaviour. ULE trains two models concurrently: a student model and a teacher model. The student is trained using standard Empirical Risk Minimisation and learns to rely on spurious correlations present in the data. Meanwhile, the teacher is trained to actively avoid these spurious correlations by minimising alignment with the student’s saliency maps. This encourages the teacher to focus on more semantically meaningful features, resulting in a model that learns a more robust feature representation. Importantly, ULE achieves this without requiring x access to group labels or prior information about spurious features, making it widely applicable in real-world scenarios. The final contribution, Weighted UnLearning from Experience (wULE), builds upon ULE by introducing a targeted sample re-weighting strategy that distinguishes between samples likely and unlikely to contain spurious correlations. Instead of treating all samples uniformly, wULE leverages the simplicity bias principle to estimate the set of training samples suspected to contain spurious correlations. The loss function is adjusted on a per-sample basis: samples in this set receive stronger penalties for gradient alignment to encourage unlearning, while cleaner samples are weighted more heavily in the classification objective to reinforce reliable feature learning. This adaptive strategy leads to improved worst-group performance and further enhances interpretability through more focused and meaningful saliency maps. Together, these contributions position explainability, not just as a diagnostic tool, but a core strategy for training resilient and robust machine learning systems.

title: Modular Abstract Interpretation for Stack-Heap Analysis of C/C++ via LLVM IR
abstract: Detecting memory errors in C/C++ by static analysis means reasoning about program values and memory structure together, but value- and memory-oriented analyses are usually combined in fixed, domain-specific ways. This work proposes a modular, parametric framework, based on abstract interpretation theory, with a split-state abstraction that separates values from memory structure into two independent, interchangeable domains. Any pair satisfying a minimal interface yields a sound combined analysis by construction. Precision can thus be adapted without redesigning the analysis, for instance by trading a coarser memory domain for a richer value one.

title: TMAC-GAN: Topology and Marker-Aware Chromatic Learning for Virtual Stain
abstract: Generating virtual immunohistochemistry (IHC) images from standard hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histopathology may support more efficient pathological assessment. However, this cross-modal image translation task is challenged by spatial misalignment in consecutive tissue sections and visual heterogeneity across biomarkers. To address these issues, we propose the Topology and Marker-Aware Chromatic Generative Adversarial Network (TMAC-GAN) for virtual staining under adjacent-section misalignment. The topology-based bidirectional contrastive learning (TBCL) module reduces dependence on strict pixel-level correspondence by aligning cross-modal representations at the region level through feature graphs. The marker-aware chromatic-textural (MACT) module addresses marker-specific visual variation through 3D color angular and gradient texture constraints that encourage chromatic consistency and subcellular boundary similarity. Evaluations on the BCI and MIST datasets show competitive perceptual and structural consistency compared with representative virtual staining methods.

title: Bi‐Gated Orthogonal Calibration for Text‐Centric Multimodal Sentiment Regression
abstract: ABSTRACT Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to predict continuous affect intensity by integrating textual, visual, and acoustic information. However, effective multimodal modeling remains challenging due to representation overlap and noise across modalities, potentially inconsistent cross‐modal cues, and the difficulty of preserving fine‐grained sentiment consistency under varying modality conditions. To address these issues, we propose a Bi‐Gated Orthogonal Calibration (BGOC) framework for text‐centric multimodal sentiment regression. title: Do Perturbation Predictors Learn Gene Interactions? Diagnosing Extrapolation in Agentic Screening
abstract: High-throughput perturbation screens increasingly use machine-learning models to predict the effects of gene combinations that were never measured. A difficult case arises when both genes in a test pair were seen individually during training, but their combination was not. In this setting, standard OOD methods often fail because neither gene appears unfamiliar on its own. We therefore compare each model prediction with a simple additive prediction obtained by summing the two observed single-gene effects. The difference between them, which we call additive disagreement (AD), measures how much extra interaction effect the model introduces for an unseen combination. Across eight prediction methods and three Perturb-seq datasets, specialised neural predictors do not consistently outperform this simple additive baseline. More importantly, predictions with larger deviations from the additive baseline tend to have larger errors. Conventional output-based and embedding-based confidence signals are inconsistent across datasets and models, whereas AD remains informative across all evaluated compositional settings. We further study how this signal can guide decisions in an agentic perturbation-screening workflow. The code is available at https://github.com/zygao930/OOD.

title: Geometry-Aware Time Reparameterization for Flow-Map Distillation
abstract: Flow-map distillation enables one- and few-step generation by learning finite-time transitions of a pretrained generative ODE. We investigate whether changing the teacher's time parameterization can make these transitions easier to learn. Motivated by the hypothesis that trajectory segments with large normal acceleration are harder to distill, we propose a geometry-aware time reparameterization that allocates more student time to these regions while preserving the teacher's geometric paths and terminal distribution. We derive a shared clock that equalizes a population normal-acceleration statistic under suitable assumptions, and construct a practical approximation from robust, regularized estimates across teacher trajectories. We incorporate this clock into Lagrangian flow-map distillation, using the transformed time coordinate to condition the student. The clock is estimated once before distillation and requires neither teacher retraining nor additional student parameters or inference-time network evaluations. Experiments on synthetic data, CIFAR-10, and CelebA-64 show improved sample quality over identity-time distillation at matched inference budgets, including improvements in one- and two-step image generation. The gains in one-step generation, where no intermediate sampling times can be adjusted, highlight the benefits of time reparameterization during distillation.

title: Loss-tolerant distributed lattice surgery using fusion networks
abstract: Networking matter-based quantum processing units (QPUs) offers a promising route to scaling fault-tolerant quantum computers. This requires distributed logical operations to be performed across photonic links, where noise is characteristically different from and stronger than in local QPUs owing to photon loss and probabilistic linear-optical operations. Measurement- and fusion-based quantum computing are designed to be robust against loss and probabilistic photonic operations, suggesting they could complement circuit-based error correction at the interface between networked QPUs. We use ZX calculus transformations to construct hybrid syndrome extraction protocols and apply them to distributed rotated surface code lattice surgery, demonstrating that several protocols attain a $50\%$ interface-erasure threshold when local noise is absent, including circuit-based lattice surgery using fused Bell pairs and hybrid protocols using linear cluster states. Relative to a straight Bell-pair interface geometry, the hybrid protocols increase the merge-observable interface distance from $d+1$ to $2d+1$ and restore the perpendicular-observable interface distance from $\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$ to $d$. We calculate how the threshold decreases when using truncated resource states and map correctable regions under resource-state errors, local circuit noise, and fusion erasure. We then convert these erasure thresholds into photon-loss thresholds and probe subthreshold performance using fusion boosting. At circuit and resource-state error rates of $10^{-3}$, local errors largely mask the interface-distance advantage. As local noise is reduced to $10^{-4}$ and below, the linear-chain protocols improve more rapidly with decreasing erasure, suggesting that interface distance enhancements are effective in low local noise regimes.

title: Communication-Efficient Improved Federated Learning Framework with Local Privacy Perturbation for Distributed Sensitive Data Privacy Preservation
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) emerges as a promising distributed machine learning paradigm, which enables collaborative model training among multiple edge clients without uploading raw sensitive data to the central server. Nevertheless, conventional federated learning systems still suffer from two intractable bottlenecks: severe privacy leakage risks caused by plaintext gradient/model parameter transmission and excessive communication overhead induced by frequent complete parameter updates across heterogeneous edge devices. To tackle the above dual challenges, this paper proposes a communication-efficient improved federated learning framework with adaptive local privacy perturbation, named Fed-LPCC (Federated Learning with Local Privacy Perturbation and Compressed Communication). First, an adaptive mixed Gaussian-Laplace local differential privacy (LDP) perturbation mechanism is designed to inject differentiated noise into local gradient updates, which dynamically adjusts noise amplitude according to gradient sensitivity and residual privacy budget, effectively preventing sensitive data leakage from gradient inversion attacks while reducing unnecessary utility loss. Second, we propose a dual-layer gradient sparsification-quantization compression strategy to eliminate redundant parameters in local updates combined with adaptive client sampling, the framework significantly cuts down uplink and downlink communication traffic during global aggregation. Furthermore, we derive rigorous privacy accounting based on Rényi Differential Privacy (RDP) and complete convergence proof for the proposed Fed-LPCC framework. Extensive comparative experiments are conducted on three mainstream public datasets (MNIST, CIFAR-10, Adult) against state-of-the-art privacy-preserving federated learning methods. The experimental results demonstrate that Fed-LPCC achieves a maximum communication compression ratio of 94.7%, reduces privacy budget consumption by 18.3% compared with traditional fixed-noise LDP-FL methods, and maintains competitive model accuracy with a maximum accuracy drop of only 2.1%. The proposed framework can well balance privacy preservation, communication efficiency and model utility, which is suitable for distributed sensitive data training scenarios in intelligent edge computing, healthcare and financial risk prediction.

title: COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS AND CLASS IMBALANCE HANDLING STRATEGIES FOR CREDIT CARD FRAUD DETECTION
abstract: Severe class imbalance complicates the evaluation of credit card fraud detection models. This study compares six classifiers under no balancing, class weighting, SMOTE, and random undersampling, yielding 24 configurations. Experiments used approximately 1.85 million synthetic Sparkov transactions with a temporal train-test split. Average Precision (AP) was the primary metric, complemented by classification and alert-budget measures.

title: We Do Care Global — Published Projects Portal & Autonomous AI Governance OS
abstract: Author portal and open-source portfolio for We Do Care Global, founded by Emir Perla in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina. The organization operates on a fundamental pledge of dedicating 33% of its annual revenue to provide financial and material assistance to vulnerable individuals worldwide for a dignified life. In technology, We Do Care Global delivers autonomous AI governance from first principles across 6 core systems: multi-agent factory orchestration (FoundationCentar), agent security and policy control planes (AgentGuard), enterprise function calling and secrets governance (AgentVault), production retrieval-augmented generation (Enterprise Hybrid-RAG with NVIDIA NeMo), agent observability and benchmarking (Agent Eval), and pharmacovigilance intelligence (Pharma Intelligence OS). Every release is archived on Zenodo with permanent DataCite DOIs under Apache-2.0 and attributed to ORCID 0009-0009-8515-2727.

title: The Herchel Smith Intellectual Property Lecture 2025
abstract: To ensure appropriate remuneration for the use of human literary and artistic works in the development and exploitation of generative AI models, both individual licensing and collective remuneration solutions have been proposed. The following analysis sheds light on the heated discussion about the best remuneration mechanism and contrasts the current trend towards individual licensing with potential advantages of collective approaches that take AI output as a reference point. An assessment of the various regulatory options in light of competing policy objectives – fair remuneration on the one hand, broad access to training resources for culturally diverse AI on the other hand – concludes the discussion.

title: Shared Representation-Guided Cross-Modal Dynamic Fusion Network for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
authors: LI Rui, HUANG Junchen, ZHANG Junzhe, DUAN Zongtao
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis aims to improve the accuracy and robustness of sentiment recognition by integrating information from textual, visual, and acoustic modalities. Compared with unimodal approaches, multimodal fusion strategies can, to some extent, mitigate the problems of incomplete and redundant information that may exist in individual modalities. However, existing methods mainly focus on modeling modality consistency or performing static cross-modal feature fusion, while paying less attention to the dynamic interaction relationships among modalities that vary with context. As a result, they struggle to fully capture the differing sentiment contributions of each modality in specific samples. To address these challenges, a multimodal sentiment analysis framework is constructed that integrates shared representation learning with a dynamic fusion mechanism. This framework initially employs pretrained models to enhance the semantic representations of raw features from each modality, improving their expressiveness in emotional contexts. Subsequently, a shared representation space is constructed to align the three modalities, establishing a unified semantic foundation that facilitates effective cross-modal interaction and collaboration. Building on this shared space, a dynamic fusion module is designed, which is guided by shared representations and incorporates cross-modal attention mechanisms alongside dynamic routing strategies. This module adaptively allocates weights to each modality based on its emotional contribution to the given input sample, enabling precise and context-aware integration of multimodal features. The fused representation is then processed through a feed-forward neural network to perform sentiment classification. Extensive experiments conducted on multiple widely used public multimodal sentiment analysis datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Results indicate significant improvements in evaluation metrics such as mean absolute error, Pearson correlation coefficient, and classification accuracy when compared with baseline approaches. Moreover, the approach demonstrates strong interpretability by explicitly revealing modality contributions and maintains robustness across diverse and complex multimodal scenarios. These findings support the applicability of the framework for real-world emotion recognition tasks involving dynamic and heterogeneous multimodal data sources.
